target.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Plugins have no typed, policy-enforced API for emitting AI safety events. Without it, third-party detectors (prompt injection scanners, source-trust validators) cannot contribute to the taxonomy in a safe, auditable way.

## Evidence
- `src/plugins/safety-event-emission.ts` (new) — `emitPluginSafetyEvent()` with trust-gated manifest policy
- External plugins must declare permitted event types in `safetyEventTypes` manifest field; undeclared types rejected at runtime
- `OpenClawPluginServiceContext.emitSafetyEvent` added to plugin service context
- `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.ts` updated as reference implementation (emits `ai_safety.external_content.consumed` on navigate)
- 16 unit tests in `src/plugins/safety-event-emission.test.ts` covering trusted/untrusted paths and manifest enforcement
- Depends on: #107176

## Evidence — Clawsweeper re-review fixes (2026-07-14)

**Emission-path fix:** with #107176 now excluding AI safety events from the untrusted `emitDiagnosticEvent()` API, manifest-authorized external plugins would have had their events silently dropped. `emitPluginSafetyEvent` now routes the authorized external path through a new core-internal `emitAuthorizedAISafetyDiagnosticEvent` (not exported from the plugin SDK), which bypasses the anti-spoofing gate only after manifest `safetyEventTypes` validation and keeps `metadata.trusted=false` so exporters (#107184) record accurate emitter provenance.

```
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — trusted plugin > emits any declared event type via trusted path
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — trusted plugin > trusted plugin can emit without declaredSafetyEventTypes
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — trusted plugin > trusted plugin can emit prompt injection signal
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — non-trusted (external) plugin > emits via authorized untrusted-provenance path when type is declared in manifest
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — non-trusted (external) plugin > rejects undeclared event type with ok: false
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — non-trusted (external) plugin > rejects when declaredSafetyEventTypes is empty
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — non-trusted (external) plugin > rejects when declaredSafetyEventTypes is absent
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — non-trusted (external) plugin > allows multiple declared types and picks the right one
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — invalid event type > rejects event type that does not start with ai_safety.
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — invalid event type > rejects unknown ai_safety.* type not in taxonomy
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — invalid event type > rejects empty string type
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — all taxonomy types accepted for trusted plugin > accepts ai_safety.prompt_injection.signal
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — all taxonomy types accepted for trusted plugin > accepts ai_safety.tool_policy.decision
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — all taxonomy types accepted for trusted plugin > accepts ai_safety.external_content.consumed
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — all taxonomy types accepted for trusted plugin > accepts ai_safety.user_feedback.received
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — all taxonomy types accepted for trusted plugin > accepts ai_safety.memory_context.selected
✓ emitPluginSafetyEvent — all taxonomy types accepted for trusted plugin > accepts ai_safety.eval.result

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  17 passed (17)
```

**4-PR series design note:** the security boundary is deliberate across the stack — #107176 defines the contracts and excludes AI safety events from the untrusted emit surface (type- and runtime-gated); #107184 wires exporters and preserves emitter provenance; this PR adds the only plugin-facing emission surface, gated by manifest `safetyEventTypes`; #107192 adds observability surfaces. Untrusted path gated, trusted path only.

**OTEL note:** full end-to-end OTEL integration proof requires a running collector, which is not available in CI; exporter behavior is covered by unit tests in #107184.
